content: 1. The use of CYP3A4 inhibitors can significantly reduce the clearance of avanafil, leading to increased systemic exposure. This heightened exposure may result in severe adverse effects such as profound hypotension, syncope, visual disturbances, and priapism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 2. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative drugs. 3. Clarithromycin elevates axitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the axitinib dose by 50%. 4. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 5. Clarithromycin reduces the efficacy of the BCG vaccine live through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is completed before administering live bacterial vaccines. 6. Clarithromycin increases bedaquiline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than 14 consecutive days unless the benefits outweigh the risks. 7. Clarithromycin enhances the effects of bemiparin by reducing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 8. Clarithromycin increases bivalirudin levels by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 9. Clarithromycin raises bosutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 10. Clarithromycin increases brigatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the brigatinib dose by 50%. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 11. Clarithromycin elevates bromocriptine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 12. Clarithromycin increases budesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 13. Clarithromycin raises buprenorphine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 14. Clarithromycin increases buspirone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 15. Clarithromycin elevates cabazitaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Clarithromycin increases cabergoline levels by reducing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Clarithromycin raises cabozantinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary, reduce the cabozantinib dose and resume the previous dose 2-3 days after discontinuing the inhibitor. 18. Clarithromycin increases calcitriol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 19. Clarithromycin elevates capivasertib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. 20. Clarithromycin increases carbamazepine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor plasma levels if used concomitantly. 21. Clarithromycin and ceritinib both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases ceritinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 22. Clarithromycin raises chloroquine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 23. Omeprazole increases cilostazol levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 24. Clarithromycin and chlorpromazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 25. Clarithromycin reduces the efficacy of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration with systemic antibiotics. Do not administer the vaccine to patients who have received antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 26. Clarithromycin increases cinacalcet levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 27. Clarithromycin and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 28. Clarithromycin and citalopram both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of toxicity. Monitor QT interval or ECG if co-administered. 29. Clarithromycin raises clomipramine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 30. Omeprazole reduces clopidogrel efficacy by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism, which is essential for clopidogrel bioactivation. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 31. Clarithromycin increases clozapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 32. Omeprazole increases dacomitinib levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 33. Clarithromycin increases colchicine levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4. Co-administration is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 34. Clarithromycin raises conjugated estrogens levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 35. Clarithromycin increases copanlisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg. 36. Clarithromycin elevates cortisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 37. Clarithromycin and crizotinib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 38. Clarithromycin increases cyclosporine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 39. Clarithromycin raises dabrafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 40. Clarithromycin enhances dalteparin effects by reducing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 41. Clarithromycin increases daridorexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 42. Clarithromycin raises darifenacin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 43. Clarithromycin increases dasatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Omeprazole reduces dasatinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 44. Clarithromycin and degarelix both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 45. Omeprazole increases digoxin levels by altering gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 46. Clarithromycin and desflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 47. Clarithromycin and desipramine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 48. Clarithromycin raises dexamethasone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 49. Clarithromycin increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 50. Clarithromycin elevates digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 51. Clarithromycin and disopyramide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 52. Clarithromycin and dofetilide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 53. Clarithromycin and donepezil both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 54. Clarithromycin and doxepin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 55. Clarithromycin increases dronedarone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 56. Clarithromycin and droperidol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 57. Clarithromycin raises edoxaban levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. 58. Clarithromycin and efavirenz both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 59. Clarithromycin increases elacestrant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 60. Clarithromycin raises elbasvir/grazoprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 61. Clarithromycin increases eletriptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Separate administration by 72 hours. 62. Clarithromycin and eliglustat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 63. Clarithromycin raises eluxadoline levels by inhibiting its metabolism. Reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID if co-administered with OATP1B1 inhibitors. 64. Clarithromycin increases elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 65. Clarithromycin raises encorafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose. 66. Clarithromycin enhances enoxaparin effects by reducing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 67. Clarithromycin and entrectinib both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases entrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 68. Clarithromycin increases enzalutamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 69. Clarithromycin and epinephrine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs.
